  • Field Details

    • LSB_FIRST

      public static final boolean LSB_FIRST
      True when the host JVM is little-endian (x86, x86_64, ARM in LE mode).

      X11 requires the client to declare its byte order in the very first byte of the connection setup request ('B' for MSB-first, 'l' for LSB-first). The server then sends every multi-byte protocol field in the client's declared order. Escher 0.2.2 was hardwired to big-endian, which only worked on SPARC/PowerPC hosts or against X servers explicitly started with -byteswappedclients. Modern Xwayland rejects byte-swapped clients by default, so the lg3d JDK-21 port makes the wire format follow the host's native order.

      When this flag is true, read2(int), read4(int), read8(int), write2(int,int), write4(int,int), and write8(int,long) reverse byte order on the wire, and Display sends 'l' in the connection setup.
